title: Rhino workflows and connector status
description: Explore Rhino workflows with Vector OS, from vessel geometry to drawing review. Rhino is available in the beta; Grasshopper integration is in development.

Explore a vessel from its first brief to drawings and review.

View options

Start with the vessel

Show a compact twin-hull utility workboat with a forward wheelhouse and a working deck aft.

A 15m twin-hull workboat has a forward wheelhouse, visible bridge deck and a readable working deck.

What changes in this example?

An authored side and deck sketch aligns with one recognizable vessel containing shaped hulls, transoms, rails, mast and five equipment groups. Brief and Reference describe the same concept rather than interchangeable marine decoration.

Changed

  • Input presentation changes between brief and reference

  • The complete baseline workboat is revealed

Retained

  • 15m illustrative length

  • 6.4m overall beam

  • Twin-hull separation

  • Forward wheelhouse

  • 12 named top-level groups

Workboat concept preview; no performance-qualified vessel design is claimed.

Read the steps

  • Read the compact workboat brief or inspect its matching sketch.

  • Align the sketch with the baseline three-quarter model.

  • Reveal both hulls, wheelhouse, working deck and named equipment as one vessel concept.

Connector status: Available. Rhino is available in the Vector OS beta. Grasshopper integration is in development; it does not inherit Rhino availability.

Rhino: Available. Rhino is available in the Vector OS beta. Grasshopper integration is in development; it does not inherit Rhino availability.

Grasshopper: In development. Grasshopper integration is in development. Rhino availability does not establish Grasshopper feature support.

Check current availability

Why use a marine example?

The workboat shows several connected tasks clearly: hull form, equipment layout, repeated sections and drawing views. Rhino and Grasshopper also serve other design fields.

Does changing the graph create permanent Rhino objects?

A preview and persisted model objects are different states. The detailed example explains the intended bake step; any persistent update path depends on the actual definition and supported integration.

Are the vessel and drawings engineering deliverables?

They explain a design workflow. Vessel calculations, detailed production documentation and engineering approval remain separate work.

How do I check Beta access and compatibility?
